```text
Current Baseline:
Primary Architectural Pressure:
Candidate Options:

Selected Front:
Reason:

Required Preconditions:
Known Risks:
Baseline Impact:
Expected Deliverable:
Explicit Non-Goals:

Decision Status:
APPROVED / PENDING
```

---

# Decision Evidence

## 33.72 Evidence sources

La decisión deberá basarse en:

```text
Sprint 22 final audit
repository state
data readiness
consumer readiness
operational priorities
```

---

## 33.73 No intuition-only decision

La intuición puede orientar.

No deberá sustituir evidencia.

---

## 33.74 Generic sequence

Cuando no exista otra presión dominante, una secuencia razonable será:

```text

        ↓

        ↓
Gateway / API
        ↓
Consumer Adapter
        ↓
Visual Interface
        ↓
Progressive Module Integration
```

## 33.75 Alternative transport-first sequence

Si ya se conoce bien la cobertura de datos:

```text

        ↓
Gateway / API
        ↓
Consumer Adapter
        ↓
Visual Slice
        ↓
Data Audit expansion
```

---

## 33.76 Alternative extensibility-first sequence

Si el riesgo principal es la generalización contractual:

```text
Materialization Baseline
        ↓
Second Capability
        ↓
Registry decision if needed
        ↓
Gateway / Consumers
```

# Decision Safeguards

## 33.77 Safeguard 1

No abrir UI si requiere bypass contractual.

---

## 33.78 Safeguard 2

No abrir Gateway si el contrato aún cambia continuamente.

---

## 33.79 Safeguard 3

No abrir segunda capability para demostrar arquitectura si una necesidad operacional más importante está bloqueada.

---

## 33.80 Safeguard 4

No abrir auditoría de datos ilimitada sin preguntas concretas por módulo.

# Sprint Naming Governance

## 33.81 Name follows pressure

El nombre del siguiente Sprint deberá reflejar su objetivo principal.

## 33.82 Good naming

Ejemplos:

```text

HEYTI Six-Module Data Readiness Audit

HEYTI Visual Interface Foundation
HEYTI Multi-Capability Materialization
```

## 33.83 Avoid vague names

Evitar:

```text
HEYTI Improvements
Next Phase
More Integration
```

## 33.87 Why

```text
Materialization Baseline v1
```

como punto de partida.

```text
baseline impact
```

```text
Final commit
```

# Decision Definition of Done

## 33.103 DoD

La decisión del siguiente Sprint estará completa cuando:

1. Sprint 22 esté técnicamente cerrado;
2. la baseline esté protegida;
3. las presiones estén identificadas;
4. los candidatos estén comparados;
5. exista una presión principal;
6. exista un Sprint seleccionado;
7. sus precondiciones estén conocidas;
8. sus riesgos estén conocidos;
9. los non-goals estén definidos;
10. exista handoff.

---

# 33.104 Declaración final del capítulo

El siguiente Sprint no deberá surgir automáticamente de la última línea de código escrita en Sprint 22.

Deberá surgir de una evaluación consciente del sistema.

La secuencia correcta será:

```text
CLOSE SPRINT 22
        ↓
PROTECT BASELINE
        ↓
OBSERVE CURRENT PRESSURES
        ↓
COMPARE OPTIONS
        ↓
IDENTIFY BLOCKER
        ↓
SELECT NEXT SPRINT
        ↓
DEFINE NON-GOALS
        ↓
BEGIN FROM VERIFIED BASELINE
```

Esto permite que la evolución de HEYTI mantenga dirección.

Por tanto:

> **A roadmap is not a list of things we could build.**

> **A roadmap is an ordered response to architectural pressure.**

Con este protocolo, cada nuevo Sprint deberá existir porque resuelve una necesidad concreta del sistema y no porque una tecnología o componente resulte atractivo en ese momento.

La Materialization Baseline deberá permanecer como punto estable.

Y el siguiente paso deberá elegirse en función de aquello que permita a HEYTI avanzar con mayor seguridad hacia:

```text
reliable knowledge
operational consumption
visual intelligence
multi-module integration
```

sin sacrificar la arquitectura ya certificada.

# Capítulo 34 — Sprint Handoff Package, Baseline Transfer and Successor Sprint Entry Contract

## 34.1 Propósito del capítulo

El cierre técnico de Sprint 22 y la selección del siguiente frente arquitectónico no serán suficientes por sí solos para garantizar continuidad.

Entre ambos deberá existir una transferencia explícita de estado.

Este capítulo establece el:

> **Sprint Handoff Package, Baseline Transfer and Successor Sprint Entry Contract**

Su propósito será asegurar que el siguiente Sprint reciba de Sprint 22:

- la baseline exacta;
- el commit de referencia;
- los contratos vigentes;
- los invariantes protegidos;
- las decisiones arquitectónicas;
- los gaps diferidos;
- las pruebas de referencia;
- los riesgos conocidos;
- los límites que no deberán romperse;
- las precondiciones necesarias para iniciar correctamente.

La meta será evitar que el Sprint sucesor tenga que reconstruir el contexto mediante memoria, inferencias o relectura desordenada del repositorio.

---

## 34.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **A Sprint is not fully handed off until the successor can identify exactly what is inherited, what is protected, what remains unresolved and what may change.**

La transición deberá ser explícita.

No:

```text
Sprint 22 ends
        ↓
new Sprint starts coding
```

Sino:

```text
Sprint 22 verified baseline
        ↓
formal handoff
        ↓
successor entry verification
        ↓
new Sprint execution
```

---

```text
What baseline do we inherit?
What guarantees are already proven?

What code implements the baseline?
What tests protect it?
What gaps remain?
What must not be changed casually?
What is the next architectural pressure?
What is the next Sprint allowed to modify?
```

## 34.87 Architecture preservation

## 34.89 DoD

El handoff estará completo cuando:

5. las garantías estén listadas;

7. el vertical slice esté identificado;
8. la regresión esté registrada;
9. los gaps estén documentados;

11. la presión siguiente esté identificada;
12. el Sprint sucesor esté seleccionado;
13. el scope esté definido;
14. los non-goals estén definidos;

# 34.92 Declaración final del capítulo

El valor de una baseline no termina cuando se certifica.

Su verdadero valor aparece cuando puede entregarse a la siguiente fase sin perder significado.

Por ello, Sprint 22 deberá terminar con una transferencia explícita:

```text
WHAT WAS BUILT
        ↓
WHAT WAS VERIFIED
        ↓
WHAT IS PROTECTED
        ↓
WHAT REMAINS
        ↓
WHAT COMES NEXT
```

El Sprint sucesor no deberá comenzar preguntando:

```text
How did Materialization work again?
```

Deberá comenzar sabiendo:

```text
Materialization Baseline v1 is verified.
These are its guarantees.
These are its protected boundaries.
These are its tests.
These are its gaps.
This is the problem I now have to solve.
```

Por tanto:

> **Technical closure proves the work.**

> **Baseline protection preserves the work.**

> **Handoff transfers the work.**

> **Successor entry continues the work without losing it.**

Con este protocolo, HEYTI podrá evolucionar Sprint tras Sprint sin convertir cada nueva fase en una reconstrucción del contexto anterior.

---

```text
SPRINT 22 — HANDOFF STATE

TECHNICAL CLOSURE:             VERIFIED
MATERIALIZATION BASELINE v1:   VERIFIED
BASELINE PROTECTION:           ACTIVE
NEXT-SPRINT FRAMEWORK:         COMPLETE
HANDOFF PACKAGE:               COMPLETE
SUCCESSOR ENTRY CONTRACT:      COMPLETE
DEFERRED GAPS:                 TRANSFERRED
PROTECTED INVARIANTS:          TRANSFERRED
TEST BASELINE:                 TRANSFERRED

SUCCESSOR SPRINT:
READY FOR SELECTION / OPENING

SPRINT 22 HANDOFF STATUS:
AUTHORIZED
```

---

# Regla final

> **Un Sprint no entrega sólo código.**

> **Entrega un estado conocido del sistema y las reglas necesarias para no destruirlo en el siguiente paso.**


# Capítulo 35 — Successor Sprint Activation, Inherited Baseline Verification and Controlled Entry to the Next Architectural Phase

## 35.1 Propósito del capítulo

Una vez completados:

```text
Sprint 22 Technical Closure
        ↓
Materialization Baseline Protection
        ↓
Next-Sprint Decision
        ↓
Handoff Package
```

deberá existir un mecanismo explícito para activar el Sprint sucesor.

Este capítulo establece:

> **Successor Sprint Activation, Inherited Baseline Verification and Controlled Entry to the Next Architectural Phase**

Su propósito será asegurar que el Sprint siguiente:

- comience desde la baseline correcta;
- verifique nuevamente el estado del repositorio;
- herede conscientemente los invariantes;
- conozca los gaps diferidos;
- confirme su alcance;
- declare sus non-goals;
- identifique cualquier drift ocurrido desde el cierre anterior;
- no modifique la baseline hasta superar su gate de entrada.

---

## 35.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **A successor Sprint SHALL verify what it inherits before it changes what it inherits.**

Por tanto, la secuencia será:

```text
HANDOFF
   ↓
INHERITED BASELINE
   ↓
RE-VERIFICATION
   ↓
SCOPE CONFIRMATION
   ↓
ENTRY GATE
   ↓
SUCCESSOR ACTIVATION
```

---

# Successor Sprint Identity

## 35.3 Sprint identity

El Sprint sucesor deberá declarar formalmente:

El nombre deberá reflejar el problema principal que resolverá.

No deberá abrirse simplemente como:

```text
Sprint 23 — Continuation
```

si existe una presión arquitectónica más precisa que pueda darle identidad.

## 35.25 Full regression

# Invariant Re-acceptance

## 35.26 Purpose

El siguiente Sprint no deberá heredar únicamente código.

Deberá aceptar conscientemente los invariantes protegidos.

---

## 35.27 Required inherited invariants

Como mínimo:

```text
Capability owns cognition.
Materializer owns contractual expression.
Validator enforces contract trust.
Runtime coordinates execution.
Consumer owns presentation.
Raw Cognitive Result is not external fallback.
Traceability is never fabricated.
Consumer bypass is prohibited.
```

---

Deberá registrarse:

```text
PROTECTED INVARIANTS:
REVIEWED AND ACCEPTED
```

antes de modificar una frontera protegida.

```text
NO LONGER RELEVANT
```

## 35.31 No automatic inheritance of priority

Un gap diferido no deberá entrar automáticamente al scope del siguiente Sprint.

# Handoff Completion Relationship

## 35.68 Sprint 22 side

Sprint 22 concludes with:

```text
HCG-22 PASS
```

---

## 35.69 Successor side

The successor begins with:

```text
SAG-01 PASS
```

---

## 35.70 Transition bridge

Thus:

```text
SPRINT 22
HCG-22
   ↓
HANDOFF
   ↓
SUCCESSOR
SBG-01
SSG-01
SIG-01
   ↓
SAG-01
```

---

# No Gap Between Governance and Execution

## 35.71 Purpose

This sequence prevents an uncontrolled interval in which:

```text
old Sprint is closed
but new Sprint has started changing code
without baseline verification
```

---

# Transition Traceability

## 35.72 Trace chain

It should be possible to reconstruct:

```text
Sprint 22 Final Commit
        ↓
Handoff Package
        ↓
Successor Initial Commit
        ↓
Successor Changes
```

---

# Baseline Mutation Detection

## 35.73 First successor commit

The first commit that modifies protected baseline elements must explicitly reveal that impact.

---

## 35.74 No hidden mutation

A change to:

```text
contracts.py
validation.py
describe_section.py
Runtime materialization integration
```

should never appear as incidental work in an unrelated commit.

---

# Successor Regression Contract

## 35.75 Inherited regression obligation

Every successor Sprint that touches HEYTI Core shall continue to satisfy:

```text
previous baseline tests
+
new Sprint tests
```

---

## 35.76 Cumulative quality model

Thus:

```text
Sprint N quality
=
Sprint N-1 guarantees
+
new verified guarantees
```

unless an explicit versioned architectural change replaces a previous guarantee.

---

# Successor Documentation Contract

## 35.77 New Sprint documentation

The successor document should begin by declaring:

```text
Inherited Baseline
Primary Pressure
Scope
Non-Goals
Protected Invariants
Entry Evidence
```

---

## 35.78 No context reset

It should not rewrite HEYTI architecture from zero.

---

# Controlled Architectural Evolution

## 35.79 Default rule

The successor should add the smallest architecture required by its pressure.

---

## 35.80 No speculative extension

It shall not introduce infrastructure only because it might be useful several Sprints later.

---

# Successor Readiness Definition

## 35.81 Ready

A Sprint successor is truly ready when:

```text
it knows where it starts
it knows what it inherits
it knows what it may change
it knows what it must preserve
it knows how success will be verified
```

---

# Transition Integrity Gate

## 35.82 TIG-01

Se establece:

> **TIG-01 — Sprint Transition Integrity Gate**

Requerirá:

```text
source Sprint closed              YES
handoff complete                  YES
successor baseline verified       YES
successor scope confirmed         YES
successor invariants accepted     YES
successor activation              PASS
```

---

# Transition Failure

## 35.83 Failure condition

Si la baseline no puede verificarse:

```text
NEXT SPRINT DEVELOPMENT:
STOP
```

---

## 35.84 Reason

No deberá construirse encima de un estado incierto.

---

# Sprint Continuity Principle

## 35.85 Rule

Se establece:

> **Every Sprint SHALL begin with a known inherited state and end with a known delivered state.**

---

## 35.86 Lifecycle implication

Esto produce:

```text
Known State A
      ↓
Controlled Change
      ↓
Known State B
      ↓
Controlled Handoff
      ↓
Known State C
```

---

# Architectural Memory through Artifacts

## 35.87 Critical principle

La continuidad deberá residir en:

```text
documents
commits
tests
contracts
baseline records
```

no sólo en conversación.

---

# Successor Activation Definition of Done

## 35.88 DoD

La activación estará completa cuando:

1. la baseline heredada esté identificada;
2. el commit fuente esté verificado;
3. el estado actual esté conocido;
4. cualquier drift esté explicado;
5. la regresión esté en PASS;
6. el vertical slice esté en PASS;
7. los invariantes estén aceptados;
8. los gaps estén revisados;
9. la presión principal esté confirmada;
10. el scope esté definido;
11. los non-goals estén definidos;
12. el impacto sobre baseline esté conocido;
13. SAG-01 esté en PASS.

---

# 35.89 Declaración final del capítulo

El valor del handoff sólo se materializa cuando la siguiente fase demuestra que realmente recibió aquello que debía recibir.

Por ello, el paso correcto no será:

```text
Sprint 22 closed
        ↓
start next coding task
```

Será:

```text
Sprint 22 closed
        ↓
baseline transferred
        ↓
baseline independently verified
        ↓
invariants re-accepted
        ↓
scope confirmed
        ↓
next Sprint activated
```

Esto convierte la transición entre Sprints en una operación auditable.

Por tanto:

> **Sprint closure protects the past.**

> **Handoff transfers the past.**

> **Successor verification proves that the past arrived intact.**

> **Successor activation authorizes the future.**

Con este mecanismo, HEYTI podrá evolucionar sin reiniciar su arquitectura en cada Sprint y sin confiar únicamente en memoria para preservar decisiones críticas.

Cada nuevo Sprint deberá comenzar sabiendo exactamente:

```text
WHAT IS TRUE
WHAT IS PROTECTED
WHAT IS PENDING
WHAT MAY CHANGE
WHAT MUST BE PROVEN NEXT
```

y sólo entonces deberá iniciar su propia transformación controlada.

---

# Estado esperado después del Capítulo 35

```text
SPRINT TRANSITION CONTROL

SPRINT 22 TECHNICAL CLOSURE:      VERIFIED
HANDOFF:                          COMPLETE
MATERIALIZATION BASELINE v1:      TRANSFERRED
SUCCESSOR BASELINE:               RE-VERIFIED
BASELINE DRIFT:                   UNDERSTOOD
PROTECTED INVARIANTS:             ACCEPTED
DEFERRED GAPS:                    REVIEWED
SUCCESSOR SCOPE:                  CONFIRMED
SUCCESSOR NON-GOALS:              CONFIRMED
SUCCESSOR ACTIVATION GATE:        PASS

SUCCESSOR SPRINT STATUS:
ACTIVE
```

---

# Regla final

> **No heredamos una baseline porque confiamos en que sigue intacta.**

> **La heredamos porque volvemos a demostrar que sigue intacta.**


# Capítulo 35 — Successor Sprint Activation, Inherited Baseline Verification and Controlled Entry to the Next Architectural Phase

## 35.1 Propósito del capítulo

Una vez completados:

```text
Sprint 22 Technical Closure
        ↓
Materialization Baseline Protection
        ↓
Next-Sprint Decision
        ↓
Handoff Package
```

deberá existir un mecanismo explícito para activar el Sprint sucesor.

Este capítulo establece:

> **Successor Sprint Activation, Inherited Baseline Verification and Controlled Entry to the Next Architectural Phase**

Su propósito será asegurar que el Sprint siguiente:

- comience desde la baseline correcta;
- verifique nuevamente el estado del repositorio;
- herede conscientemente los invariantes;
- conozca los gaps diferidos;
- confirme su alcance;
- declare sus non-goals;
- identifique cualquier drift ocurrido desde el cierre anterior;
- no modifique la baseline hasta superar su gate de entrada.

---

## 35.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **A successor Sprint SHALL verify what it inherits before it changes what it inherits.**

Por tanto, la secuencia será:

```text
HANDOFF
   ↓
INHERITED BASELINE
   ↓
RE-VERIFICATION
   ↓
SCOPE CONFIRMATION
   ↓
ENTRY GATE
   ↓
SUCCESSOR ACTIVATION
```

---

## 35.3 Sprint identity

```text
SPRINT NAME:
PRIMARY ARCHITECTURAL PRESSURE:
SOURCE BASELINE:

```

El nombre deberá reflejar el problema principal que resolverá.

```text
Response Contract v1.0          PASS
Serialization                   PASS

Gateway baseline                INSPECTED
Transport requirements          DEFINED
```

## 35.63 Gateway first objective

El primer objetivo sería:

```text
transport existing validated contract
```

No:

```text
redesign materialization
```

```text
what HEYTI can actually know
```

por cada módulo.

```text
HEYTI Multi-Capability Materialization
```

debería comenzar:

antes de modificar materialización.

## 35.69 Successor side

# No Gap Between Governance and Execution

## 35.71 Purpose

This sequence prevents an uncontrolled interval in which:

```text
old Sprint is closed
but new Sprint has started changing code
without baseline verification
```

# Transition Traceability

## 35.72 Trace chain

It should be possible to reconstruct:

```text
Sprint 22 Final Commit
        ↓

        ↓

Successor Changes
```

# Baseline Mutation Detection

## 35.73 First successor commit

The first commit that modifies protected baseline elements must explicitly reveal that impact.

## 35.74 No hidden mutation

A change to:

```text
contracts.py
validation.py
describe_section.py
Runtime materialization integration
```

should never appear as incidental work in an unrelated commit.

# Successor Regression Contract

## 35.75 Inherited regression obligation

Every successor Sprint that touches HEYTI Core shall continue to satisfy:

```text
previous baseline tests
+
new Sprint tests
```

---

## 35.76 Cumulative quality model

Thus:

```text
Sprint N quality
=
Sprint N-1 guarantees
+
new verified guarantees
```

unless an explicit versioned architectural change replaces a previous guarantee.

## 35.77 New Sprint documentation

The successor document should begin by declaring:

```text
Inherited Baseline
Primary Pressure
Scope
Non-Goals
Protected Invariants
Entry Evidence
```

## 35.78 No context reset

It should not rewrite HEYTI architecture from zero.

# Controlled Architectural Evolution

## 35.79 Default rule

The successor should add the smallest architecture required by its pressure.

---

## 35.80 No speculative extension

It shall not introduce infrastructure only because it might be useful several Sprints later.

# Successor Readiness Definition

## 35.81 Ready

A Sprint successor is truly ready when:

```text
it knows where it starts
it knows what it inherits
it knows what it may change
it knows what it must preserve
it knows how success will be verified
```

# Transition Integrity Gate

## 35.82 TIG-01

Se establece:

> **TIG-01 — Sprint Transition Integrity Gate**

Requerirá:

```text
source Sprint closed              YES

successor baseline verified       YES
successor scope confirmed         YES
successor invariants accepted     YES
successor activation              PASS
```

# Transition Failure

## 35.83 Failure condition

Si la baseline no puede verificarse:

```text
NEXT SPRINT DEVELOPMENT:
STOP
```

---

## 35.84 Reason

No deberá construirse encima de un estado incierto.

---

# Sprint Continuity Principle

## 35.85 Rule

Se establece:

> **Every Sprint SHALL begin with a known inherited state and end with a known delivered state.**

---

## 35.86 Lifecycle implication

Esto produce:

```text
Known State A
      ↓
Controlled Change
      ↓
Known State B
      ↓
Controlled Handoff
      ↓

```

# Architectural Memory through Artifacts

## 35.87 Critical principle

La continuidad deberá residir en:

```text
documents
commits
tests
contracts
baseline records
```

no sólo en conversación.

---

# Successor Activation Definition of Done

## 35.88 DoD

La activación estará completa cuando:

1. la baseline heredada esté identificada;
2. el commit fuente esté verificado;
3. el estado actual esté conocido;
4. cualquier drift esté explicado;
5. la regresión esté en PASS;
6. el vertical slice esté en PASS;
7. los invariantes estén aceptados;
8. los gaps estén revisados;
9. la presión principal esté confirmada;
10. el scope esté definido;
11. los non-goals estén definidos;
12. el impacto sobre baseline esté conocido;
13. SAG-01 esté en PASS.

---

# 35.89 Declaración final del capítulo

El valor del handoff sólo se materializa cuando la siguiente fase demuestra que realmente recibió aquello que debía recibir.

Por ello, el paso correcto no será:

```text
Sprint 22 closed
        ↓
start next coding task
```

Será:

```text
Sprint 22 closed
        ↓
baseline transferred
        ↓
baseline independently verified
        ↓
invariants re-accepted
        ↓
scope confirmed
        ↓
next Sprint activated
```

Esto convierte la transición entre Sprints en una operación auditable.

Por tanto:

> **Sprint closure protects the past.**

> **Handoff transfers the past.**

> **Successor verification proves that the past arrived intact.**

> **Successor activation authorizes the future.**

Con este mecanismo, HEYTI podrá evolucionar sin reiniciar su arquitectura en cada Sprint y sin confiar únicamente en memoria para preservar decisiones críticas.

Cada nuevo Sprint deberá comenzar sabiendo exactamente:

```text
WHAT IS TRUE
WHAT IS PROTECTED
WHAT IS PENDING
WHAT MAY CHANGE
WHAT MUST BE PROVEN NEXT
```

y sólo entonces deberá iniciar su propia transformación controlada.

---

```text
HANDOFF:                          COMPLETE
MATERIALIZATION BASELINE v1:      TRANSFERRED
SUCCESSOR BASELINE:               RE-VERIFIED
BASELINE DRIFT:                   UNDERSTOOD
PROTECTED INVARIANTS:             ACCEPTED
DEFERRED GAPS:                    REVIEWED
SUCCESSOR SCOPE:                  CONFIRMED
SUCCESSOR NON-GOALS:              CONFIRMED
SUCCESSOR ACTIVATION GATE:        PASS

SUCCESSOR SPRINT STATUS:
ACTIVE
```

# Regla final

> **No heredamos una baseline porque confiamos en que sigue intacta.**

> **La heredamos porque volvemos a demostrar que sigue intacta.**


# Capítulo 36 — Successor Sprint Execution Governance, Change Accountability and Cumulative Baseline Preservation

## 36.1 Propósito del capítulo

Una vez que el Sprint sucesor ha sido:

```text
selected
handed off
re-verified
activated
```

comienza una nueva etapa de riesgo.

El sistema ya no necesita únicamente proteger la baseline de Sprint 22.

Necesita garantizar que cada cambio posterior:

```text
preserves
extends
or explicitly evolves
```

aquello que ya fue demostrado.

Este capítulo establece:

> **Successor Sprint Execution Governance, Change Accountability and Cumulative Baseline Preservation**

Su propósito será definir cómo deberá trabajar cualquier Sprint posterior sobre una baseline HEYTI previamente certificada.

---

## 36.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **Every successor change SHALL either preserve the inherited baseline or explicitly declare how it evolves it.**

No deberá existir una tercera opción basada en:

```text
silent drift
```

---

# Cumulative Baseline Model

## 36.3 Baseline inheritance

Cada Sprint deberá comenzar desde una baseline previamente conocida.

Conceptualmente:

```text
Baseline N
    ↓
Successor Sprint
    ↓
Baseline N+1
```

---

## 36.4 Baseline accumulation

La nueva baseline deberá contener:

```text
previous verified guarantees
+
new verified guarantees
```

salvo que exista una modificación arquitectónica explícita y versionada.

---

## 36.5 No reset model

No deberá operar así:

```text
new Sprint
→ forget previous guarantees
→ build new implementation
```

---

## 36.6 Correct model

Deberá operar:

```text
inherit
↓
verify
↓
extend
↓
test
↓
audit
↓
certify
```

---

# Change Accountability

## 36.7 Every significant change accountable

Todo cambio significativo deberá poder responder:

```text
Why was this changed?
What baseline element does it affect?
What guarantee does it add?
What existing guarantee could it break?
How was it tested?
```

---

## 36.8 No anonymous architectural change

No deberá existir un cambio arquitectónico cuyo origen sea simplemente:

```text
implementation cleanup
```

si en realidad altera comportamiento contractual.

---

# Successor Change Record

## 36.9 Minimal record

Para cambios relevantes podrá mantenerse:

```text
CHANGE:
REASON:
BASELINE IMPACT:
FILES:
TESTS:
RESULT:
```

---

## 36.10 Proportional governance

No será necesario registrar formalmente cada línea de código.

La gobernanza deberá concentrarse en cambios con impacto sobre:

```text
contracts
boundaries
responsibilities
data exposure
runtime behavior
consumer behavior
```

---

# Change Classes

## 36.11 INTERNAL

Un cambio interno no modifica comportamiento observable.

Ejemplos:

```text
private helper refactor
performance optimization
code organization
```

---

## 36.12 COMPATIBLE

Extiende comportamiento sin romper consumidores existentes.

---

## 36.13 PROFILE EXTENSION

Añade nuevas posibilidades dentro de una capability o profile existente.

---

## 36.14 BREAKING

Modifica una garantía externa existente.

---

## 36.15 ARCHITECTURAL

Modifica:

```text
responsibility
dependency direction
boundary
contract family
execution architecture
```

---

# Change Classification Gate

## 36.16 CCG-01

Se establece:

> **CCG-01 — Successor Change Classification Gate**

Antes de implementar un cambio que afecte baseline deberá existir:

```text
classification       KNOWN
reason               KNOWN
baseline impact      KNOWN
contract impact      KNOWN
test impact          KNOWN
```

---

# Inherited Guarantee Matrix

## 36.17 Guarantee ledger

Cada Sprint sucesor deberá conocer las garantías heredadas.

Por ejemplo:

| Guarantee | Source Sprint | Protected Test | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Response Contract validates | Sprint 22 | `...` | PASS |
| DescribeSection materializes | Sprint 22 | `...` | PASS |
| Runtime vertical slice works | Sprint 22 | `...` | PASS |
| Raw fallback prohibited | Sprint 22 | `...` | PASS |

## 36.18 New guarantee addition

Cada nueva garantía deberá agregarse a esta visión acumulativa.

---

# Test Accumulation Model

## 36.19 Previous tests remain

Los tests heredados deberán permanecer activos.

---

## 36.20 New tests add protection

El Sprint nuevo deberá añadir pruebas de sus nuevas garantías.

---

## 36.21 Test deletion

Una prueba heredada sólo deberá eliminarse cuando:

```text
guarantee intentionally retired
```

y exista una decisión explícita.

---

## 36.22 No green-by-deletion

Se prohíbe:

```text

→ delete test
→ suite green
```

sin revisar la garantía que protegía.

## 36.23 Layer 1 — Local

Después de un cambio:

```text
nearest tests
```

---

## 36.24 Layer 2 — Component

Después:

```text
component suite
```

---

## 36.25 Layer 3 — Protected baseline

```text
protected inherited tests
```

---

## 36.26 Layer 4 — Full regression

Finalmente:

```text
full suite
```

## 36.27 BIC-01

```text
new guarantee PASS
```

## 36.28 Failure

## 36.41 Cognitive need

Si el significado todavía no existe:

## 36.50 No Portal cognitive reconstruction

```text
new tests                     PASS
full regression               PASS
baseline impact               DOCUMENTED
```

---

# Successor Sprint Definition of Done

## 36.104 General DoD

Un Sprint sucesor que herede Materialization Baseline v1 deberá poder demostrar:

1. que partió de la baseline correcta;
2. que la verificó;
3. que clasificó sus cambios;
4. que mantuvo scope;
5. que agregó una garantía concreta;
6. que probó esa garantía;
7. que preservó garantías heredadas;
8. que auditó cambios protegidos;
9. que documentó cualquier evolución;
10. que dejó una nueva baseline conocida.

---

# Relationship with Sprint 22

## 36.105 Sprint 22 contribution

Sprint 22 establece el primer modelo formal de:

```text
baseline
→ protection
→ handoff
→ inheritance
```

---

## 36.106 Successor responsibility

Los Sprints posteriores deberán preservar esta disciplina.

---

# Cumulative Architecture Model

## 36.107 Model

La evolución de HEYTI deberá comportarse como:

```text
Architecture A
     ↓
Verified Baseline A
     ↓
Controlled Change
     ↓
Architecture A+
     ↓
Verified Baseline B
```

No como:

```text
Architecture A
     ↓
uncontrolled changes
     ↓
unknown system
```

---

# Quality Accumulation

## 36.108 Quality equation

Conceptualmente:

```text
HEYTI Quality at Sprint N
=
Verified Guarantees from Previous Sprints
+
New Verified Guarantees
-
Explicitly Retired Guarantees
```

---

# No Quality Amnesia

## 36.109 Rule

Se establece:

> **A new Sprint SHALL NOT forget why old tests, contracts or boundaries exist.**

---

# Baseline Preservation as Development Discipline

## 36.110 Meaning

La baseline no deberá sentirse como una restricción administrativa.

Deberá funcionar como una herramienta para permitir cambios con confianza.

---

# 36.111 Declaración final del capítulo

Una arquitectura sólida no se demuestra únicamente cuando se construye correctamente una vez.

Se demuestra cuando puede seguir evolucionando sin destruir sus propias garantías.

Por ello, después de Sprint 22 la pregunta ya no será únicamente:

```text
Does Materialization still work?
```

Será:

```text
Did our new change preserve everything Materialization already guaranteed?
```

La evolución correcta deberá seguir:

```text
INHERITED BASELINE
        ↓
CLASSIFIED CHANGE
        ↓
SMALL IMPLEMENTATION
        ↓
TARGETED VERIFICATION
        ↓
INHERITED REGRESSION
        ↓
FULL REGRESSION
        ↓
AUDIT
        ↓
NEW KNOWN BASELINE
```

De esta manera:

> **Every Sprint receives trust.**

> **Every Sprint must preserve or explicitly evolve that trust.**

> **Every Sprint adds evidence.**

> **Every Sprint returns a new known state.**

Con este modelo, HEYTI podrá crecer sin que su complejidad acumulada destruya la capacidad de comprender qué garantiza cada componente y por qué.

La arquitectura dejará de ser únicamente una estructura diseñada.

Se convertirá en una **cadena acumulativa de estados verificados**.

---

# Estado esperado después del Capítulo 36

```text
HEYTI — CUMULATIVE BASELINE GOVERNANCE

INHERITED BASELINE:             VERIFIED
CHANGE CLASSIFICATION:          ACTIVE
SCOPE CONTROL:                  ACTIVE
PROTECTED TESTS:                ACTIVE
CUMULATIVE REGRESSION:          ACTIVE
BASELINE IMPACT REVIEW:         REQUIRED
ARCHITECTURAL DRIFT CONTROL:    ACTIVE
SUCCESSOR AUDIT:                REQUIRED
BASELINE PROMOTION:             GOVERNED

DEVELOPMENT MODEL:
KNOWN STATE
→ CONTROLLED CHANGE
→ VERIFIED STATE
```

---

# Regla final

> **HEYTI no deberá avanzar sustituyendo certezas por novedades.**

> **Deberá avanzar convirtiendo cada novedad en una nueva certeza verificable.**


# Capítulo 37 — Long-Term Baseline Registry, Certification Ledger and Architectural Continuity Record

## 37.1 Propósito del capítulo

A medida que HEYTI acumule Sprints, contratos, capabilities, materializadores y consumidores, una simple secuencia de commits dejará de ser suficiente para comprender qué estado del sistema fue considerado estable en cada momento.

Este capítulo establece el:

> **Long-Term Baseline Registry, Certification Ledger and Architectural Continuity Record**

Su propósito será definir un registro histórico capaz de responder:

```text
Which HEYTI baseline was active?
Which Sprint created it?
Which commit certified it?
Which contracts were active?
Which guarantees were verified?
Which tests protected it?
Which gaps remained?
Which baseline replaced it?
```

La meta será preservar la continuidad arquitectónica a lo largo del tiempo.

---

## 37.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **Every certified HEYTI baseline SHOULD remain historically identifiable even after a newer baseline becomes active.**

Una baseline anterior podrá dejar de ser:

```text
CURRENT
```

pero no deberá desaparecer de la historia técnica.

---

# Baseline Registry Concept

## 37.3 Registry purpose

El Baseline Registry deberá funcionar como un catálogo conceptual de estados verificados.

---

## 37.4 Not Runtime Registry

No deberá confundirse con:

```text
CapabilityRegistry
MaterializationRegistry
```

Este registro pertenece a:

```text
engineering governance
```

no a ejecución runtime.

---

## 37.5 Registry contents

Conceptualmente podrá contener entradas como:

```text
Baseline ID
Name
Source Sprint
Commit
Date
Status
Contracts
Reference Tests
Verified Guarantees
Deferred Gaps
Successor Baseline
```

---

# Baseline Identity

## 37.6 Unique identifier

Cada baseline deberá poseer una identidad inequívoca.

Ejemplo conceptual:

```text
HEYTI-BL-MAT-001
```

---

## 37.7 Human-readable name

Además podrá mantener:

```text
HEYTI Materialization Baseline v1
```

---

## 37.8 ID versus name

El ID facilita trazabilidad.

El nombre facilita comunicación.

---

# Baseline Status Vocabulary

## 37.9 Status values

Las baselines podrán clasificarse como:

```text
ACTIVE
SUPERSEDED
RETIRED
INVALIDATED
HISTORICAL
```

según necesidad.

---

## 37.10 ACTIVE

Representa la baseline vigente para una arquitectura específica.

---

## 37.11 SUPERSEDED

Significa que existe una baseline posterior que la reemplaza como referencia activa.

---

## 37.12 RETIRED

Significa que la baseline ya no deberá utilizarse para nuevas implementaciones.

---

## 37.13 INVALIDATED

Sólo deberá utilizarse si se descubre que una baseline certificada contenía una falla crítica que invalida su garantía.

---

## 37.14 HISTORICAL

Podrá utilizarse para baselines preservadas únicamente como referencia histórica.

---

# Baseline Certification Ledger

## 37.15 Ledger purpose

El Certification Ledger deberá registrar la evidencia principal utilizada para certificar cada baseline.

---

## 37.16 Ledger fields

```text
Sprint:
Certification Date:
Final Commit:
Full Regression:
Vertical Slice:
Contract Version:
Blocking Gaps:
Unknown Gaps:
Certification Gate:
```

---

## 37.17 Evidence-first rule

Ninguna entrada deberá marcarse:

```text
CERTIFIED
```

sin evidencia real.

## 37.18 Source Sprint

Cada baseline deberá identificar el Sprint que la produjo.

No será obligatorio registrar cada checkpoint intermedio como baseline histórica permanente.

# Baseline Registry Readiness Gate

## 37.106 BRRG-01

Se establece:

> **BRRG-01 — Baseline Registry Governance Ready**

Requerirá:

```text

```

# 37.107 Declaración final del capítulo

El desarrollo de HEYTI no deberá conservar únicamente una historia de cambios.

Deberá conservar una historia de certezas verificadas.

Git podrá responder:

```text
What changed?
```

Los documentos podrán responder:

```text
Why was it designed this way?
```

Los tests podrán responder:

```text
What behavior was proven?
```

Y el Baseline Registry deberá responder:

```text
Which combination of design, code and tests was formally considered a trusted HEYTI state?
```

La evolución completa podrá representarse como:

```text
DESIGN
   ↓
IMPLEMENTATION
   ↓
VERIFICATION
   ↓
CERTIFIED BASELINE
   ↓
CONTROLLED EVOLUTION
   ↓
NEXT CERTIFIED BASELINE
```

Por tanto:

> **A commit records code history.**

> **A Sprint records engineering intent.**

> **A test records behavioral evidence.**

> **A certified baseline records a trusted state.**

Con este mecanismo, HEYTI podrá crecer durante años sin perder la capacidad de reconstruir cuáles fueron sus estados estables, qué garantizaban y cómo evolucionaron.

---

```text
HEYTI Materialization Baseline v1
```

# Regla final

> **HEYTI no sólo deberá recordar qué cambió.**

> **Deberá recordar qué estados fueron suficientemente confiables como para construir el futuro sobre ellos.**


# Capítulo 38 — Baseline Registry Operationalization, Certification Workflow and Historical Query Protocol

## 38.1 Propósito del capítulo

El Capítulo 37 definió el concepto de:

> **Long-Term Baseline Registry**

como registro histórico de estados verificados de HEYTI.

Sin embargo, para que dicho Registry sea útil deberá existir una forma controlada de:

```text
create baseline entry
validate baseline evidence
certify baseline
activate baseline
supersede baseline
invalidate baseline
query baseline history
```

Este capítulo establece:

> **Baseline Registry Operationalization, Certification Workflow and Historical Query Protocol**

como protocolo operativo para administrar futuras baselines de HEYTI.

---

## 38.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **A baseline registry entry SHALL represent verified engineering state, not project narration.**

El Registry deberá registrar hechos demostrables.

No expectativas.

No planes.

No memoria informal.

---

# Registry Operational Model

## 38.3 Lifecycle

Toda baseline podrá atravesar conceptualmente:

```text
CANDIDATE
    ↓
VERIFICATION
    ↓
CERTIFIED
    ↓
ACTIVE
    ↓
SUPERSEDED
```

con posibles rutas excepcionales hacia:

```text
INVALIDATED
RETIRED
HISTORICAL
```

---

# Candidate Baseline

## 38.4 Definition

Una baseline será:

```text
CANDIDATE
```

cuando exista un estado de repositorio propuesto para certificación.

---

## 38.5 Candidate requirements

Como mínimo deberá conocerse:

```text
source Sprint
repository
branch
commit
scope
expected guarantees
```

---

## 38.6 Candidate is not trusted baseline

Una baseline candidata todavía no deberá utilizarse como referencia certificada.

---

# Verification State

## 38.7 Verification

Durante:

```text
VERIFICATION
```

deberán comprobarse:

```text
tests
contracts
invariants
gaps
repository state
documentation alignment
```

---

## 38.8 No certification before evidence

El estado:

```text
CERTIFIED
```

no deberá asignarse antes de completar esta verificación.

---

# Certified Baseline

## 38.9 Meaning

Una baseline:

```text
CERTIFIED
```

ha demostrado sus garantías mediante evidencia.

---

## 38.10 Certification does not automatically mean active

Podría existir una baseline certificada preparada para sustituir otra, pero todavía no ser la referencia activa.

---

# Active Baseline

## 38.11 ACTIVE

La baseline activa será la referencia de ingeniería para nuevas modificaciones dentro de su alcance.

---

## 38.12 One active baseline per scope

Como regla general deberá existir:

```text
one ACTIVE baseline
```

por alcance arquitectónico.

---

## 38.13 Example

Conceptualmente:

```text
Materialization Baseline
ACTIVE = v1
```

---

# Superseded Baseline

## 38.14 SUPERSEDED

Cuando una baseline posterior se convierta en activa, la anterior podrá quedar:

```text
SUPERSEDED
```

---

## 38.15 Superseded does not mean invalid

Significa:

```text
historically valid
but no longer current
```

---

# Retired Baseline

## 38.16 RETIRED

Podrá utilizarse cuando una arquitectura o contrato ya no deba emplearse para nuevas implementaciones.

---

# Invalidated Baseline

## 38.17 INVALIDATED

Se utilizará únicamente cuando exista evidencia de que una baseline certificada contenía una falla que invalida una garantía fundamental.

---

## 38.18 High threshold

No deberá marcarse una baseline como invalidada por:

```text
minor bug
cosmetic issue
later design preference
```

---

# Historical Baseline

## 38.19 HISTORICAL

Una baseline podrá conservarse con este estado cuando su valor sea principalmente documental y de trazabilidad.

---

# Certification Workflow

## 38.20 Workflow overview

La certificación deberá seguir:

```text
Candidate identified
      ↓
Evidence collected
      ↓
Tests executed
      ↓
Guarantees reviewed
      ↓
Gaps reviewed
      ↓
Commit confirmed
      ↓
Certification Gate
      ↓
Registry Entry
```

---

# Step 1 — Candidate Identification

## 38.21 Candidate declaration

Deberá registrarse:

```text
Baseline Candidate ID:
Source Sprint:
Scope:
Candidate Commit:
```

---

## 38.22 Immutable candidate commit

Durante la certificación deberá evitarse que el commit candidato cambie silenciosamente.

---

## 38.23 New change during certification

Si aparece un cambio necesario:

```text
new commit
```

deberá actualizarse el candidato y repetir la evidencia afectada.

---

# Step 2 — Repository Evidence

## 38.24 Required repository evidence

Deberá registrarse:

```text
Repository:
Branch:
Commit:
Working Tree:
```

---

## 38.25 Working tree requirement

La condición preferente será:

```text
CLEAN
```

---

# Step 3 — Environment Evidence

## 38.26 Required environment data

Cuando corresponda:

```text
Python:
pytest:
Package version:
```

---

# Step 4 — Test Evidence

## 38.27 Required test record

Deberá registrarse:

```text
Collected:
Passed:
Failed:
Errors:
Skipped:
Warnings:
```

---

## 38.28 Certification condition

Como regla general:

```text
FAILED = 0
ERRORS = 0
```

---

# Step 5 — Guarantee Evidence

## 38.29 Guarantee review

Cada garantía candidata deberá contar con evidencia.

---

## 38.30 Guarantee table

Podrá utilizarse:

| Guarantee | Evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `...` | test/code/audit | PASS |

---

## 38.31 No unsupported guarantee

Una garantía sin evidencia deberá eliminarse del alcance o bloquear certificación.

---

# Step 6 — Contract Evidence

## 38.32 Contract record

Deberá identificarse:

```text
Contract ID:
Contract Version:
Profiles:
```

cuando existan.

---

## 38.33 Contract compatibility

Si la baseline sustituye otra deberá registrarse:

```text
compatible
breaking
not applicable
```

---

# Step 7 — Gap Evidence

## 38.34 Gap review

Deberán registrarse:

```text
Blocking:
Unknown:
Deferred:
```

---

## 38.35 Certification requirement

Deberá cumplirse:

```text
Blocking = 0
Unknown = 0
```

---

# Step 8 — Invariant Review

## 38.36 Relevant invariants

Deberán revisarse los invariantes aplicables al alcance.

---

## 38.37 Not every HEYTI invariant every time

La revisión deberá ser proporcional.

---

# Step 9 — Documentation Alignment

## 38.38 Documentation check

Deberá verificarse que la baseline tenga documentación suficiente para explicar:

```text
what changed
what is guaranteed
what remains
```

---

# Step 10 — Certification Decision

## 38.39 Decision

La baseline deberá quedar:

```text
CERTIFIED
```

o:

```text
REJECTED
```

---

## 38.40 No partial certification ambiguity

Si algunas garantías no pueden demostrarse deberá reducirse explícitamente el scope o rechazar certificación.

---

# Certification Gate

## 38.41 BCG-CERT-01

Se establece:

> **BCG-CERT-01 — Baseline Certification Gate**

Requerirá:

```text
candidate commit             KNOWN
working tree                 CLEAN
test state                   PASS
guarantees                   VERIFIED
contract state               KNOWN
blocking gaps                ZERO
unknown gaps                 ZERO
documentation                ALIGNED
```

---

# Registry Entry Creation

## 38.42 After certification

Sólo después de BCG-CERT-01 deberá crearse o actualizarse la entrada definitiva del Registry.

---

## 38.43 Registry Entry ID

Deberá asignarse una identidad única.

---

## 38.44 Example

```text
HEYTI-BL-MAT-001
```

---

# Entry Structure

## 38.45 Required core fields

Una entrada operativa deberá contener:

```text
ID
Name
Status
Scope
Source Sprint
Parent Baseline
Commit
Contracts
Guarantees
Tests
Gaps
Certification Date
```

---

# Activation Workflow

## 38.46 Activation

Si la baseline certificada debe convertirse en referencia activa:

```text
CERTIFIED
    ↓
ACTIVE
```

---

## 38.47 Previous active baseline

La baseline anterior deberá actualizarse a:

```text
SUPERSEDED
```

cuando corresponda.

---

# Activation Atomicity

## 38.48 Rule

La activación deberá evitar estados contradictorios como:

```text
v1 ACTIVE
v2 ACTIVE
```

para el mismo scope sin justificación.

---

# Baseline Parent Relationship

## 38.49 Parent

Toda baseline evolutiva deberá indicar su baseline padre.

---

## 38.50 First baseline

Podrá utilizar:

```text
Parent = NONE
```

---

# Supersession Workflow

## 38.51 Sequence

Conceptualmente:

```text
Baseline A ACTIVE
        ↓
Baseline B CERTIFIED
        ↓
Baseline B ACTIVATED
        ↓
Baseline A SUPERSEDED
```

---

# No Retroactive Mutation

## 38.52 Historical integrity

No deberá modificarse la entrada de Baseline A para que parezca haber garantizado algo que sólo apareció en Baseline B.

---

# Invalidation Workflow

## 38.53 Trigger

Podrá iniciarse cuando se descubre:

```text
critical defect
false certification assumption
broken foundational guarantee
```

---

## 38.54 Investigation first

No deberá invalidarse inmediatamente sin reproducir y comprender la falla.

---

## 38.55 Invalidation record

Deberá registrarse:

```text
Reason:
Evidence:
Affected Guarantees:
Corrective Baseline:
```

cuando exista.

---

# Corrective Baseline

## 38.56 Purpose

Una baseline correctiva deberá reparar la garantía sin reescribir la historia.

---

# Retirement Workflow

## 38.57 Retirement trigger

Podrá utilizarse cuando:

```text
architecture removed
contract unsupported
subsystem replaced
```

---

# Historical Query Protocol

## 38.58 Purpose

El Registry deberá permitir consultas reproducibles sobre la evolución de HEYTI.

---

## 38.59 Query type 1

```text
What baseline is currently active?
```

---

## 38.60 Expected answer

Debe poder obtenerse:

```text
Baseline ID
Name
Commit
Status
```

---

# Query type 2

## 38.61 Historical state query

```text
What baseline was active after Sprint X?
```

---

## 38.62 Answer

Deberá incluir:

```text
baseline
commit
contracts
major guarantees
```

---

# Query type 3

## 38.63 Contract origin query

```text
Which baseline introduced Response Contract v1.0?
```

---

# Query type 4

## 38.64 Capability support query

```text
Which baseline first materialized DescribeSection?
```

---

# Query type 5

## 38.65 Guarantee origin query

```text
When was raw fallback formally prohibited and verified?
```

---

# Query type 6

## 38.66 Gap history query

```text
When did GAP-X appear?
When was it resolved?
```

---

# Query type 7

## 38.67 Baseline lineage query

```text
What baseline replaced BL-001?
```

---

# Query type 8

## 38.68 Invalidated baseline query

```text
Was any certified baseline later invalidated?
Why?
```

---

# Query Result Discipline

## 38.69 No guessing

Historical queries shall be answered from Registry evidence.

---

## 38.70 Unknown result

If the Registry cannot answer:

```text
NOT RECORDED
```

shall be preferable to reconstruction by assumption.

---

# Registry Search Index

## 38.71 Future convenience

The Registry may later support indexes by:

```text
Sprint
contract
capability
baseline ID
date
status
```

---

## 38.72 Not required initially

Simple Markdown navigation may be sufficient.

---

# Registry Update Protocol

## 38.73 When to update

The Registry should be updated when:

```text
new baseline certified
baseline activated
baseline superseded
baseline invalidated
baseline retired
```

---

## 38.74 When not to update

Not for:

```text
ordinary code commit
minor bug fix before certification
daily development state
```

---

# Entry Validation

## 38.75 Registry consistency

An entry should not contain contradictions such as:

```text
Status = ACTIVE
Successor = ACTIVE newer baseline
```

without explanation.

---

# Registry Consistency Checks

## 38.76 Check 1

Every ACTIVE baseline has certification evidence.

---

## 38.77 Check 2

Every SUPERSEDED baseline identifies a successor where possible.

---

## 38.78 Check 3

Every baseline references a real commit.

---

## 38.79 Check 4

Every listed contract version existed in that baseline.

---

## 38.80 Check 5

Every listed guarantee has evidence.

---

# Registry Consistency Gate

## 38.81 RCG-LT-01

Se establece:

> **RCG-LT-01 — Baseline Registry Consistency Gate**

Requerirá:

```text
baseline IDs unique           YES
active pointers consistent    YES
commit references valid       YES
lineage consistent            YES
guarantees evidenced          YES
status transitions valid      YES
```

---

# Baseline Promotion Workflow

## 38.82 Candidate to active

The complete path shall be:

```text
CANDIDATE
    ↓
VERIFICATION
    ↓
CERTIFIED
    ↓
ACTIVE
```

---

## 38.83 No direct promotion

Avoid:

```text
new commit
→ ACTIVE baseline
```

without certification.

---

# Baseline Audit Replay

## 38.84 Future capability

A mature process may permit replaying baseline certification by checking out the corresponding commit and executing the reference tests.

---

## 38.85 Purpose

This would strengthen reproducibility.

---

## 38.86 Not mandatory now

It should not be automated prematurely.

---

# Tagging Workflow Future

## 38.87 Trigger

When the number of significant baselines grows, Git tags may improve traceability.

---

## 38.88 Tag requirements

Any future tag should point to the exact certified commit.

---

# Registry versus Release Management

## 38.89 Distinction

The Baseline Registry is not necessarily a release system.

---

## 38.90 Baseline can exist without product release

A subsystem may have a certified baseline before HEYTI is externally released.

---

# Registry versus Semantic Versioning

## 38.91 Distinction

Baseline numbering does not need to follow contract semantic versioning.

---

# Registry Query for Onboarding

## 38.92 Recommended first question

A new developer should be able to ask:

```text
What is the current verified HEYTI baseline relevant to my work?
```

---

# Registry Query for Audit

## 38.93 Recommended audit question

An auditor should be able to ask:

```text
What evidence certified this architecture?
```

---

# Registry Query for Debugging

## 38.94 Debug use

A developer may ask:

```text
Did this behavior already exist in the previous baseline?
```

---

# Diff Between Baselines

## 38.95 Baseline comparison

A useful future operation will be:

```text
Baseline B
-
Baseline A
=
Verified architectural delta
```

---

## 38.96 Delta categories

Could include:

```text
new guarantees
changed guarantees
new contracts
new capabilities
resolved gaps
new risks
```

---

# Baseline Delta Record

## 38.97 Template

```text
BASELINE DELTA

FROM:
TO:

NEW GUARANTEES:
CHANGED GUARANTEES:
RETIRED GUARANTEES:

NEW CONTRACTS:
CHANGED CONTRACTS:

NEW CAPABILITIES:

RESOLVED GAPS:
NEW GAPS:

ARCHITECTURAL CHANGES:
```

---

# Historical Query Integrity

## 38.98 Rule

Se establece:

> **Historical baseline queries SHALL describe what was verified at that time, not what later became true.**

---

# Baseline Registry as Governance Memory

## 38.99 Purpose

The Registry becomes a persistent engineering memory of HEYTI's certified states.

---

# Registry Scope Control

## 38.100 Avoid noise

Not every temporary implementation state should become a baseline.

---

## 38.101 Baseline worthiness

A baseline should be registered when it is meaningful as a future reference point.

---

# Baseline Worthiness Questions

## 38.102 Questions

```text
Does this state establish a new verified capability?
Does it define a stable contract boundary?
Will future work depend on it?
Would we want to return to this state?
Does it represent a meaningful architectural milestone?
```

---

## 38.103 If mostly no

It probably does not need a permanent Registry entry.

---

# Registry Operational Roles

## 38.104 Developer

Uses it to understand current trusted state.

---

## 38.105 Architect

Uses it to trace architectural evolution.

---

## 38.106 Auditor

Uses it to connect guarantees to evidence.

---

## 38.107 Maintainer

Uses it to understand lineage and compatibility.

---

# Materialization Baseline v1 Operational Entry

## 38.108 Planned workflow

When Sprint 22 is really executed:

```text
Candidate:
HEYTI Materialization Baseline v1

Verification:
Sprint 22 FIAG-22

Certification:
TCG-22 PASS

Registry Entry:
HEYTI-BL-MAT-001

Status:
ACTIVE
```

---

## 38.109 Important condition

This entry must not be created as:

```text
CERTIFIED
```

until real implementation evidence exists.

---

# Registry Creation Timing

## 38.110 Right moment

The physical Registry should preferably be created:

```text
when the first real certified baseline exists
```

rather than filled with hypothetical entries.

---

# First Registry Entry Gate

## 38.111 FREG-01

Se establece:

> **FREG-01 — First HEYTI Baseline Registry Entry Gate**

Requerirá:

```text
real certified baseline       YES
real commit                   YES
real test evidence            YES
real guarantees               YES
real gaps                     YES
```

---

# Registry Maintenance Burden Control

## 38.112 Principle

The Registry must remain useful enough that it is actually maintained.

---

## 38.113 Avoid over-detail

It should reference detailed evidence instead of copying it.

---

# Operational Baseline Registry Definition of Done

## 38.114 DoD

La operacionalización estará definida cuando:

1. exista lifecycle;
2. exista workflow de certificación;
3. exista workflow de activación;
4. exista workflow de supersession;
5. exista workflow de invalidación;
6. exista workflow de retiro;
7. exista protocolo de consulta histórica;
8. exista consistencia del Registry;
9. exista baseline delta;
10. exista gate para primera entrada real.

---

# 38.115 Declaración final del capítulo

Un Registry de baselines sólo tendrá valor si puede utilizarse operacionalmente.

No deberá convertirse en una lista de hitos escritos después de los hechos.

Su función será conectar:

```text
CANDIDATE STATE
        ↓
VERIFICATION
        ↓
CERTIFICATION
        ↓
ACTIVE BASELINE
        ↓
CONTROLLED SUCCESSION
        ↓
HISTORICAL TRACE
```

Gracias a este flujo, HEYTI podrá responder no sólo:

```text
What is our current architecture?
```

sino también:

```text
When did it become trusted?
What evidence made it trusted?
What did it replace?
What eventually replaced it?
```

Por tanto:

> **The Registry records trust transitions.**

> **The Ledger records certification evidence.**

> **The lineage records architectural continuity.**

> **Historical queries reconstruct HEYTI's verified evolution.**

Con este mecanismo, cada baseline podrá convertirse en un estado técnico identificable, reproducible y auditable dentro de la historia completa del HEYTI Core.

---

# Estado esperado después del Capítulo 38

```text
HEYTI — BASELINE REGISTRY OPERATION

BASELINE LIFECYCLE:             DEFINED
CERTIFICATION WORKFLOW:         DEFINED
ACTIVATION WORKFLOW:            DEFINED
SUPERSESSION WORKFLOW:          DEFINED
INVALIDATION WORKFLOW:          DEFINED
RETIREMENT WORKFLOW:            DEFINED
HISTORICAL QUERY PROTOCOL:      DEFINED
BASELINE DELTA MODEL:           DEFINED
REGISTRY CONSISTENCY GATE:      DEFINED
FIRST REAL ENTRY GATE:          DEFINED

FIRST PLANNED CERTIFIED ENTRY:
HEYTI-BL-MAT-001
HEYTI Materialization Baseline v1
```

---

# Regla final

> **Una baseline no se vuelve parte de la historia de HEYTI cuando se escribe su nombre.**

> **Se vuelve parte de la historia cuando existe evidencia suficiente para certificar que realmente fue un estado confiable del sistema.**


# Capítulo 39 — Master Traceability Integration, Documentation Lineage and Certified Baseline Navigation Model

## 39.1 Propósito del capítulo

Sprint 22 ha definido una arquitectura completa de:

```text
Materialization
Contracts
Context
Validation
Mapping
Runtime Integration
Testing
Audit
Baseline Certification
Baseline Protection
Handoff
Baseline Registry
```

Sin embargo, todos estos elementos deberán integrarse posteriormente dentro de una estructura mayor de navegación documental.

Este capítulo establece:

> **Master Traceability Integration, Documentation Lineage and Certified Baseline Navigation Model**

como puente formal entre Sprint 22 y el futuro:

> **Mapa Maestro de Consulta y Trazabilidad Documental de HEYTI**

Su propósito será definir cómo deberá leerse, rastrearse y auditarse la historia completa de la Materialization Layer desde su origen normativo hasta su implementación certificada.

---

## 39.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **Every important HEYTI implementation SHALL be traceable backward to its architectural intent and forward to its executable evidence.**

La trazabilidad deberá funcionar en ambas direcciones:

```text
WHY
↓
DESIGN
↓
CODE
↓
TEST
↓
BASELINE
```

y:

```text
BASELINE
↓
TEST
↓
CODE
↓
DESIGN
↓
WHY
```

---

# Traceability Purpose

## 39.3 Primary objective

El sistema documental deberá permitir responder:

```text
Where did this architectural rule come from?
Which document defined it?
Which code implements it?
Which test verifies it?
Which commit certified it?
Which baseline contains it?
```

---

## 39.4 No isolated artifact

Ningún artefacto crítico deberá quedar aislado.

Por ejemplo:

```text
test
```

sin conocer qué garantía protege.

O:

```text
contract
```

sin conocer qué estándar lo definió.

---

# Materialization Traceability Chain

## 39.5 Canonical chain

La Materialization Layer deberá poder recorrerse así:

```text
HEYTI Architecture
        ↓
Materialization Standards — HMS
        ↓
Sprint 22
        ↓
Materialization Source Code
        ↓
Materialization Tests
        ↓
Runtime Integration
        ↓
Final Audit
        ↓
Certified Baseline
        ↓
Successor Sprint
```

---

# Normative Origin

## 39.6 HMS

La fuente normativa principal será:

```text
HEYTI Materialization Standards — HMS
```

---

## 39.7 HMS role

HMS deberá responder:

```text
What must Materialization guarantee?
```

---

# Implementation Architecture

## 39.8 Sprint 22 role

Sprint 22 deberá responder:

```text
How will those guarantees be implemented?
```

---

## 39.9 Code role

El código deberá responder:

```text
Where and how were they implemented?
```

---

## 39.10 Test role

Los tests deberán responder:

```text
How was implementation behavior verified?
```

---

## 39.11 Baseline role

La baseline deberá responder:

```text
Which verified implementation state became trusted?
```

---

# Traceability Dimensions

## 39.12 Required dimensions

La trazabilidad deberá operar al menos sobre:

```text
Requirement
Architecture
Implementation
Test
Commit
Baseline
Evolution
```

# Final Traceability Gate

## 39.98 FTG-MAT-01

Se establece:

> **FTG-MAT-01 — Materialization Traceability Completeness Gate**

Requerirá:

```text

```

---

# 39.99 Declaración final del capítulo

HEYTI no deberá depender de una sola forma de memoria.

El código recuerda implementación.

Git recuerda cambios.

Los tests recuerdan garantías.

Los documentos recuerdan intención.

Las baselines recuerdan estados confiables.

El Mapa Maestro deberá conectar todas esas memorias.

La cadena completa será:

```text
ARCHITECTURAL INTENT
        ↓
NORMATIVE STANDARD
        ↓
SPRINT DESIGN
        ↓
IMPLEMENTATION
        ↓
TEST EVIDENCE
        ↓
CERTIFIED BASELINE
        ↓
SUCCESSOR EVOLUTION
```

Y deberá poder recorrerse también en sentido contrario.

Por tanto:

> **Traceability is the ability to explain how a trusted system state came to exist.**

> **Documentation lineage explains why each layer exists.**

> **Baseline navigation explains which implementation became trusted.**

> **The Master Traceability Map connects the entire engineering history.**

Con este modelo, la Materialization Layer de HEYTI no quedará únicamente implementada y certificada.

Quedará también integrada a una arquitectura documental capaz de explicar su origen, su ejecución, su verificación y su evolución futura.


# Capítulo 40 — Materialization Knowledge Transfer, Operational Onboarding and Maintainer Readiness Protocol

## 40.1 Propósito del capítulo

La arquitectura de Materialization de HEYTI podrá considerarse verdaderamente sostenible únicamente cuando pueda ser comprendida, operada, auditada y modificada por personas que no participaron directamente en su diseño original.

Este capítulo establece:

> **Materialization Knowledge Transfer, Operational Onboarding and Maintainer Readiness Protocol**

Su propósito será definir cómo deberá transferirse el conocimiento técnico y arquitectónico relacionado con:

```text
Materialization
Response Contracts
Validation
DescribeSection Mapping
Runtime Integration
Testing
Baselines
Traceability
Change Governance
```

a futuros:

```text
developers
maintainers
reviewers
auditors
architects
```

---

## 40.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **A maintainable architecture MUST be understandable without relying on the memory of its original authors.**

Por tanto, el conocimiento crítico deberá residir en:

```text
documents
code
tests
baseline records
traceability artifacts
```

y no exclusivamente en:

```text
conversation
oral explanation
personal memory
```

---

# Knowledge Transfer Objective

## 40.3 Objective

Una persona nueva deberá poder responder, después de seguir el onboarding:

```text
What is Materialization?
Why does it exist?
Where does it live?
What does it consume?
What does it produce?
What does it validate?
How does Runtime invoke it?
How is DescribeSection mapped?
How is failure handled?
How is the baseline protected?
How do I safely modify it?
```

# 40.115 Declaración final del capítulo

La arquitectura sólo alcanza madurez cuando deja de depender de quienes la recuerdan.

Sprint 22 deberá producir no únicamente:

```text
Materialization Code
```

sino un sistema de conocimiento capaz de explicar:

```text
WHY IT EXISTS
WHAT IT GUARANTEES
WHERE IT LIVES
HOW IT WORKS
HOW IT FAILS
HOW IT IS TESTED
HOW IT MAY CHANGE
WHAT MUST REMAIN TRUE
```

La ruta de transferencia deberá ser:

```text
ARCHITECTURE
      ↓
STANDARD
      ↓
SPRINT
      ↓
CODE
      ↓
TESTS
      ↓
BASELINE
      ↓
TRACEABILITY
      ↓
ONBOARDING
      ↓
MAINTAINER
```

De esta forma, una persona nueva no tendrá que convertirse en arqueólogo del repositorio antes de poder colaborar.

Tendrá un camino.

Y ese camino deberá conducir desde la intención arquitectónica hasta la evidencia ejecutable.

Por tanto:

> **Documentation preserves intent.**

> **Code preserves implementation.**

> **Tests preserve guarantees.**

> **Baselines preserve trusted states.**

> **Traceability connects them.**

> **Onboarding transfers them to the next person.**

Con este protocolo, Materialization podrá dejar de ser conocimiento de una sesión o de un pequeño grupo y convertirse en conocimiento operacional permanente del HEYTI Core.

# Capítulo 40 — Materialization Knowledge Transfer, Operational Onboarding and Maintainer Readiness Protocol

## 40.1 Propósito del capítulo

La arquitectura de Materialization de HEYTI podrá considerarse verdaderamente sostenible únicamente cuando pueda ser comprendida, operada, auditada y modificada por personas que no participaron directamente en su diseño original.

Este capítulo establece:

> **Materialization Knowledge Transfer, Operational Onboarding and Maintainer Readiness Protocol**

Su propósito será definir cómo deberá transferirse el conocimiento técnico y arquitectónico relacionado con:

```text
Materialization
Response Contracts
Validation
DescribeSection Mapping
Runtime Integration
Testing
Baselines
Traceability
Change Governance
```

a futuros:

```text
developers
maintainers
reviewers
auditors
architects
```

---

## 40.2 Principio rector

Se establece:

> **A maintainable architecture MUST be understandable without relying on the memory of its original authors.**

Por tanto, el conocimiento crítico deberá residir en:

```text
documents
code
tests
baseline records
traceability artifacts
```

y no exclusivamente en:

```text
conversation
oral explanation
personal memory
```

---

# Knowledge Transfer Objective

## 40.3 Objective

Una persona nueva deberá poder responder, después de seguir el onboarding:

```text
What is Materialization?
Why does it exist?
Where does it live?
What does it consume?
What does it produce?
What does it validate?
How does Runtime invoke it?
How is DescribeSection mapped?
How is failure handled?
How is the baseline protected?
How do I safely modify it?
```

# Long-Term Maintenance Principle

## 40.111 Principle

Se establece:

# Architectural Folklore

## 40.112 Definition

Ocurre cuando reglas críticas existen sólo como:

```text
"we always do it this way"
```

sin fuente localizable.

# Folklore Remediation

## 40.113 Action

```text
document
test
baseline
```

según corresponda.

# Knowledge Continuity

## 40.114 Long-term objective

Si los autores originales no están disponibles, HEYTI deberá seguir siendo:

```text
understandable
testable
maintainable
auditable
```

---

# 40.115 Declaración final del capítulo

La arquitectura sólo alcanza madurez cuando deja de depender de quienes la recuerdan.

Sprint 22 deberá producir no únicamente:

```text
Materialization Code
```

sino un sistema de conocimiento capaz de explicar:

```text
WHY IT EXISTS
WHAT IT GUARANTEES
WHERE IT LIVES
HOW IT WORKS
HOW IT FAILS
HOW IT IS TESTED
HOW IT MAY CHANGE
WHAT MUST REMAIN TRUE
```

La ruta de transferencia deberá ser:

```text
ARCHITECTURE
      ↓
STANDARD
      ↓
SPRINT
      ↓
CODE
      ↓
TESTS
      ↓
BASELINE
      ↓
TRACEABILITY
      ↓
ONBOARDING
      ↓
MAINTAINER
```

De esta forma, una persona nueva no tendrá que convertirse en arqueólogo del repositorio antes de poder colaborar.

Tendrá un camino.

Y ese camino deberá conducir desde la intención arquitectónica hasta la evidencia ejecutable.

Por tanto:

> **Documentation preserves intent.**

> **Code preserves implementation.**

> **Tests preserve guarantees.**

> **Baselines preserve trusted states.**

> **Traceability connects them.**

> **Onboarding transfers them to the next person.**

Con este protocolo, Materialization podrá dejar de ser conocimiento de una sesión o de un pequeño grupo y convertirse en conocimiento operacional permanente del HEYTI Core.
